newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks end down ahead of Greenspan speech.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks end down ahead of Greenspan speech.

text.p: Australian shares drifted to a lower close on Tuesday on some cautionary profit-taking in resource issues ahead of a speech by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan later in the day.
The key market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, closed 13.9 points down at 2,430.3, near its intra-day low of 2,427.9.
Early weakness was inspired by bellwether stock BHP, which surprised the market late on Monday with a news of a temporary shutdown of a blast furnace at its Port Kembla steelworks.
BHP shares ended 25 cents lower at A$18.35 (US$14.31).
"Local investors are always nervous about the possibility of big correction on Wall Street," a Melbourne dealer said.
"Basically, every time Greenspan speaks the market holds its breath and that's what it did today."
The dealer said turnover remained subdued, with most investors happy to wait on the sidelines without anticipating the direction of Greenspan's impact on U.S. markets.

"The outlook for the Australian market is still reasonably positive in the medium term, even if there is a correction on Wall Street, otherwise I think the volume of selling would have been greater today," he said.
Gold miners weakened after the price of gold resumed its fall back towards the US$350 an ounce level.

Industrial issues faired better, with the bank sector buoyed by the sustained rise of Commonwealth Bank stock as market talk continued that the bank may pay a special dividend. Commonwealth Bank shares closed nine cents firmer at A$12.77.
